# Breakscale

> A discrete-event system design simulator for learning how distributed systems
> behave under load. Build a topology, push traffic through it, and watch real
> queueing behaviour: latency percentiles, queue backlogs, and failure cascades.

Everything runs in the browser. No account, no backend, nothing leaves the page.

## What it is for

Most system design material is static diagrams and rules of thumb. Breakscale
runs the experiment instead. Load an example, drag the traffic up, and watch a
system fail in the specific way that example is about.

## What makes the numbers trustworthy

- Requests are real objects moving through the topology, occupying finite
  server slots and waiting in real FIFO queues.
- Latency percentiles come from measured request latencies, never from a mean
  multiplied by a constant.
- Abandoned work still burns capacity: when a caller times out, the downstream
  keeps working on a request nobody is waiting for. That is why retry storms
  are visible here rather than theoretical.
- The simulation is deterministic. The same seed and topology replay exactly.

## What is in it

- 33 components: load balancers, caches, databases, queues, workers, CDNs,
  rate limiters, circuit breakers, read replicas, sharded stores, autoscalers,
  stream brokers, WebSocket gateways, serverless functions, bulkheads and more.
- 23 worked examples, each isolating one failure mode, including reconstructions
  of Netflix, Spotify, Discord, Uber, Twitter/X, Stripe and WhatsApp.
- Chaos controls: crash a component, slow it, force errors, or cut a link.
- A 100-term glossary explaining every metric and what it means in practice.
  Readable as plain HTML at https://breakscale.vercel.app/glossary
